Baltic Exchange Market Report 15 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2484 (130)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3964 (293)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1948 (48)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1371 (27)
Baltic Handysize Index: 715 (9)
CAPESIZE
The market delivered another strong performance today, with both basins extending gains and reinforcing the positive momentum seen throughout the week. The BCI 182 5TC surged by $2,658 to settle at $35,953, reflecting broad-based strength across the key routes. In the Pacific, sentiment remained firmly positive, supported by steady demand and continued miner presence, with two majors active on C5. Rates pushed higher, with C5 rising by $0.450 to $13.530. Offers began the day around $14.00, though fixtures were ultimately concluded in the $13.40–$13.50 range, with operators reportedly bidding $13.50 for early May towards the close. The Atlantic basin also maintained its upward trajectory, with C3 climbing $0.586 to $32.441. Stronger activity out of South Brazil and West Africa to China underpinned gains, with fixtures reported at $32.50–$32.75 levels, while tightening tonnage supply in the North Atlantic drove firmer trans-Atlantic rates. This strength was reflected in C8, which jumped $6,531 to $32,969.
PANAMAX
A more positive day across the markets, with the Baltic Index publishing upward valuations on all routes. In the Atlantic, positive sentiment continued as bids edged higher, while offers remained scarce or firm. That said, the growing tonnage list in the Continent cannot be ignored, particularly against the backdrop of limited cargo supply from the US Gulf and US East Coast. The P1A increased by $432 to $13,891. Fronthaul activity is also reflecting this firmer sentiment, with a healthy volume of EC South America fixtures reported today. In Asia, Australian and Indonesian cargo flows remain steady, supporting tonnage demand and resulting in vessels fixing at improved levels compared to previous days. This is also having a knock-on effect on P4, with some market participants noting increased demand for tonnage on this route, alongside a growing appetite to cover stems via period employment. The P5TC increased by $427 to close at $17,528.

Atlantic
The scrubber-fitted Sargas (82,167 2026) open Haldia 2 April, was reported fixed to Cofco for an East Coast South America trip to Singapore–Japan range at $22,000, although it remains unclear how the scrubber benefit was apportioned. The Kypros Land (77,060 2014) open Jorf Lasfar 16 April, was also reported fixed for a transatlantic run, with further details unavailable.

Asia
The SM Samcheonpo (80,943 2019) open Surabaya fixed on subjects as did the Star Sapphire (82,044 2019) open Rizhao 18–23 April, though further details have yet to emerge. The Harvest (73,691 2005) open Vung Tau 21 August was also fixed on subjects for a trip from Indonesia to South Korea with rate and charterer undisclosed. Meanwhile, Damico covered a South Kalimantan to Philippines requirement on subjects basis 18 April onwards, and DAT similarly placed a vessel on subjects for an Indonesian to South Korea trade basis 27 April onwards with further details still awaited. Messrs Jindal Steel were reported to have covered two voyage requirements with Oldendorff: one for a coal stem from East Coast Australia to East Coast India at $21.50 (laycan unknown), and another for limestone from China to East Coast India for 20–25 April dates in the upper $12.00s, both with 1.25% total commission.
SUPRAMAX
The US Gulf remained in strong demand today as brokers spoke of better levels of enquiry both for trans Atlantic and fronthaul. Some said that close to midish $20,000s was being achieved for the ultramax size although actual fixing information remained scarce. A difference of opinion from the South Atlantic as some felt that the recent gains seen had reached a ceiling although others felt upward movement was still being seen, however again little in the way of fixing information surfaced. No change in fundamentals from the Continent-Mediterranean which again was described as lacking fresh impetus. The Asian arena also gained traction as brokers said that demand remained both from the NoPac and for backhaul. Further south, prompt tonnage remained tight again leading to upward pressure on rates. The 11TC average finished up $342 at $17,330.
HANDYSIZE
Another positive day for the sector, with firm sentiment observed across both the Atlantic and Asian markets. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained subdued and largely positional, with rates holding in line with previous fixtures. In the South Atlantic and US Gulf, although reported fixing activity was limited, both owners and charterers were indicating levels above previously concluded deals, reflecting underlying market strength. In Asia, sentiment continued to improve, with brokers noting stronger demand and tightening tonnage availability. The Uni Harmony (37,655 2016), open West Australia, was placed on subjects for a trip to China at around $17,000 by Berge. The New Momentum (39,042 2018), open Singapore, fixed for a trip to the Far East at approximately $15,000. Additionally, a 34,000-dwt vessel open in South Korea was heard on subjects for a trip to the Philippines at around $12,000, though further details were not disclosed. Reflecting these regional dynamics, the 7TC average rose by $167 to close at $12,875.

Market Fundamentals
Ferrexpo iron ore output falls on Russo-Ukrainian attacks

Ferrexpo’s iron ore production fell 72.1% year-on-year and 44.8% quarter-on-quarter to 592,751 tonnes in 1q26, according to the company’s announcement on Wednesday morning. This decline came as production was suspended due to nationwide attacks on Ukrainian electricity generation and transmission infrastructure during the period. Production partially resumed at reduced capacity levels in late-February 2026. One pellet line remains in operation, and the company continues to use its own fleet of rail wagons to export to Eastern and Central Europe.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA market continued to accelerate on the upside in response to a stronger physical market. The Apr contract gained the most on close with pays up to 30600, followed buy the May and June with 35150 and 34750 trading. At the same time 35000 was paid on the May+Jun strip, with the May v Jun spread widening and strengthening up to +500. Q2 was thin with 33100 paid, while the Q3 went through in volume up to 31500 and Q4 31250. Activity on the Cal27 was strong again, trading between 25750 and 26000.

PMX
PMX paper opened strong in line with the cape rally, Apr+May paid up to 20200, but this strength did not carry into the afternoon, with prices easing across the curve despite a firm physical. May fell from 20200 to a low of 19300, Jun sold down to 19500, while Jul traded between 19750 and 19100. Q3 moved from 19100 to 18700, while Q4 also eased from 17350 to 17000, with the Cal seeing very little interest on the day. Overall, the market failed to hold early gains and drifted lower across the curve into the close.

SMX + HANDY
SMX Paper came under pressure in the afternoon session, despite opening the day trading at levels above yesterdays close and a positive physical index print of +$342 (S10TC $15,296). Apr traded $15,500 down to $15,250 and closing at the lows. May opened the trading +$250 on opening levels, before trading down to $17,050 with lows of $16,900. Jun followed suit, closing just off the lows of $17,000 with earlier highs of $17,500. Q2 rarely featured, trading between $16,800-$16,700, closing down at $16,450 (-$250). Q3 attracted a fair amount of attention with a range of $400 for the day, trading $16,700 down to $16,300. Q4 traded $15,500 down to $15,150 (-$275). The Cal27 strip traded up to highs of $13,150, valued down -$200 for the day at $12,900.

Carbon
EUAs futures retraced some of yesterday's gains, mainly in the afternoon trading session, falling 0.9% on lower-than-average volumes. The benchmark Dec26 contract was trading at �74.16/eua during the assessment window, down �0.70 from yesterday. Market volumes remained light, with fewer than 20m EUAs traded.

Today's Commitment of Traders report, through last week, indicated another slight increase in the net long positions held by Investment Funds, reaching 34.7m EUAs. This is still a shadow of the 126m EUAs held in mid-January, but is up from a recent low of 32.4m at the end of March.

Market Fundamentals
Ferrexpo iron ore output falls on Russo-Ukrainian attacks
Ferrexpo’s iron ore production fell 72.1% year-on-year and
44.8% quarter-on-quarter to 592,751 tonnes in 1q26,
according to the company’s announcement on Wednesday
morning. This decline came as production was suspended
due to nationwide attacks on Ukrainian electricity generation
and transmission infrastructure during the period.
Production partially resumed at reduced capacity levels in
late-February 2026. One pellet line remains in operation, and
the company continues to use its own ﬂeet of rail wagons to
export to Eastern and Central Europe.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA market continued to accelerate on the upside
in response to a stronger physical market. The Apr contract
gained the most on close with pays up to 30600, followed
buy the May and June with 35150 and 34750 trading. At the
same time 35000 was paid on the May+Jun strip, with the
May v Jun spread widening and strengthening up to +500.
Q2 was thin with 33100 paid, while the Q3 went through in
volume up to 31500 and Q4 31250. Activity on the Cal27 was
strong again, trading between 25750 and 26000.
PMX
PMX paper opened strong in line with the cape rally,
Apr+May paid up to 20200, but this strength did not carry
into the afternoon, with prices easing across the curve
despite a ﬁrm physical. May fell from 20200 to a low of
19300, Jun sold down to 19500, while Jul traded between
19750 and 19100. Q3 moved from 19100 to 18700, while Q4
also eased from 17350 to 17000, with the Cal seeing very
little interest on the day. Overall, the market failed to hold
early gains and drifted lower across the curve into the close.

despite opening the day trading at levels above yesterdays
close and a positive physical index print of +$342 (S10TC
$15,296). Apr traded $15,500 down to $15,250 and closing at
the lows. May opened the trading +$250 on opening levels,

highs of $17,500. Q2 rarely featured, trading between

attracted a fair amount of attention with a range of $400 for
the day, trading $16,700 down to $16,300. Q4 traded $15,500

This decline came as production was suspended due to nationwide attacks on Ukrainian electricity generation and transmission infrastructure during the period. Production partially resumed at reduced capacity levels in late-February 2026. One pellet line remains in operation, and the company continues to use its own fleet of rail wagons to export to Eastern and Central Europe. Trading Commentary Cape The Cape FFA market continued to accelerate on the upside in response to a stronger physical market. The Apr contract gained the most on close with pays up to 30600, followed buy the May and June with 35150 and 34750 trading. At the same time 35000 was paid on the May+Jun strip, with the May v Jun spread widening and strengthening up to +500. Q2 was thin with 33100 paid, while the Q3 went through in volume up to 31500 and Q4 31250. Activity on the Cal27 was strong again, trading between 25750 and 26000. PMX PMX paper opened strong in line with the cape rally, Apr+May paid up to 20200, but this strength did not carry into the afternoon, with prices easing across the curve despite a firm physical. May fell from 20200 to a low of 19300, Jun sold down to 19500, while Jul traded between 19750 and 19100. Q3 moved from 19100 to 18700, while Q4 also eased from 17350 to 17000, with the Cal seeing very little interest on the day. Overall, the market failed to hold early gains and drifted lower across the curve into the close. Apr traded $15,500 down to $15,250 and closing at the lows. May opened the trading +$250 on opening levels, before trading down to $17,050 with lows of $16,900. Q3 attracted a fair amount of attention with a range of $400 for the day, trading $16,700 down to $16,300. Q4 traded $15,500 down to $15,150 (-$275).
